newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares edge up, A shares lose ground.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares edge up, A shares lose ground.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly higher in slow trade on Friday on sharp gains by retailer Shenzhen International Enterprise and appliance maker Tsann Kuen with institutions sidelined, brokers said.
The B share index edged up 0.55 points, or 0.61 percent, to close at 89.58, but turnover contracted to HK$8.61 million from HK$24.07 million on Thursday.
Brokers said the rise was due in part to steep gains by Shenzhen International and Tsann Kuen.
The retailer was the sharpest gainer on speculative buying, brokers said, surging HK$0.48, or 19.05 percent, to HK$3.00 after 63,100 shares changed hands.
Tsann Kuen, Thursday's biggest loser, rallied HK$0.30, or 14.29 percent, to HK$2.40 on volume of 14,800 shares.
"Trading was so sluggish that light buying, or selling of one or two counters can significantly affect the B share index," a Shenzhen-based analyst said.
The 90-point level appears to be a short-term resistence point, another analyst said. The market will continue to see sluggish trade next week without further stimulus, he said.
Washing machine maker Little Swan jumped HK$0.03 to HK$5.43 in the day's second most active trade of 253,500 shares.

Chiwan Petroleum, the sharpest loser, fell HK$0.10, or 2.94 percent, to HK$3.30 on a single trade of 600 shares. Dadonghai continued its downward trend and traded the most on volume of 988,500 shares to close off HK$0.02 at HK$1.32.
Gujing Distillery, the strongest performer on Thursday, fell HK$0.09 to HK$5.60, with 221,950 shares traded.
The A share market tumbled as profit-taking took its toll following steady advances over recent sessions, brokers said.

The A share index slid 15.07 points, or 4.01 percent, to end at 360.52 on turnover of 13.03 billion yuan, compared with Thursday's 14.20 billion yuan. The composite index lost 13.32 points, or 3.82 percent, to end at 335.66.
Northeast Electric, which skyrocketed 108.77 percent on Thursday, dived 3.65 yuan, or 24.35 percent, to 11.34 yuan on trade volume of 15.31 million shares.
Hotelier Shijiazhuang International followed suit, plummeting 2.66 yuan, or 21.03 percent, to 9.99 yuan.
